home_faq_screen_time_desc: Screen Time has an Ignore Limit button, and a tired thumb finds it. This has no button. Once the profile is locked, the apps and their websites are gone until you erase the iPhone.
home_faq_supervision_desc: A device mode Apple built for schools and companies. A supervised iPhone accepts settings a normal one refuses: hiding apps, and a profile that cannot be removed. Everything else about the phone stays the same.
home_faq_trial_desc: Yes. Trial mode installs the same blocks, but you can remove them in Settings. It costs the same $29, because the supervision is the same. Once the iPhone is supervised, new profiles are free: to lock the blocks for good later, plug it into the Mac once more, with no new supervision and no charge.
home_faq_choice_desc: The app keeps everything on the iPhone and costs $29 per supervision. Doing it yourself is free, but Apple Configurator erases the iPhone first, so you set it up again as new and only what syncs to iCloud comes back.
home_faq_data_desc: Not with the app. It copies your iPhone to your Mac, flips one flag in the copy, then restores it to the same phone, so photos, messages and logins stay. Apps re-download, and an encrypted copy keeps your saved passwords, Health and keychain, so fewer of them ask you to sign in again. The App Store stays on and only the apps you list disappear. Doing it yourself erases the iPhone, so back it up first.
home_faq_fail_desc: The app tells you what stopped and how to fix it, then offers Try Again. It keeps its copy of your iPhone on your Mac until your blocks are on, so a restore that stopped is sent again without copying the phone a second time. It never touches your own Finder backups. Your key is spent only when supervision goes through, so a run that fails costs nothing.
home_faq_see_term: Can anyone see or track my phone?
home_faq_see_desc: No. Supervision is a flag, not a connection; remote control needs an MDM server, and you enrol in none. The profile is a fixed, signed file: once installed, nobody can change it or read anything back.
home_faq_undo_desc: With a permanent profile, only by erasing the iPhone. Supervision is enforced by iOS, so the app cannot take it back off; you can add restrictions any time, but cannot loosen or remove one without erasing. Erase from Settings, then restore from iCloud or your local backup. In trial mode, remove the profile in Settings.
home_faq_mac_desc: Yes, for one afternoon. The app needs Apple Silicon and macOS 14 or newer. Borrow a friend's Mac: the app runs from Downloads and nothing stays on it. The phone needs no Mac afterwards; going from trial mode to permanent takes one more plug-in.
home_faq_other_platforms_desc: iPhone only today, from a Mac. Windows support is planned, since the same copy works through iTunes. Android needs a different build, a small device-owner app, and is planned too.
home_story_people: I meet a lot of people, and I help many of them with their work. Most people's problems come down to one thing: not being able to do hard things. When I checked their screen time, I mostly saw 6 hours and more.
home_story_shot_friend_1: A friend's Screen Time: 6 hours 38 minutes a day on average, September 14 to 21
home_story_attention: I'm {aware} that {attention} is the most valuable thing I have. Billion-dollar companies build feeds to take it, and my willpower runs out by the afternoon like everyone else's.
home_story_path: This summer I read “{post}” by Stepan Parunashvili, about turning an iPhone into a dumbphone with Apple Configurator. It worked, but the App Store was off, my bank app broke and I couldn't scan a QR menu at a restaurant. So I wrote a guide that keeps the App Store on and blocks only the feeds. It was too long and too hard for most people, and it erased their phone first. So I built a Mac app that does the same thing in one afternoon, without erasing anything.

guide_description: The free, do-it-yourself way to a supervised, feed-free iPhone: Apple Configurator on a Mac, then a profile that blocks the feeds. It erases the iPhone.
guide_title: Supervise your iPhone yourself, for free
guide_lead: The do-it-yourself way to a feed-free iPhone. Apple Configurator on a Mac supervises the phone, then a profile blocks the apps and sites you choose.
guide_erase_body: Apple Configurator can only supervise an iPhone by erasing it. Then you set it up again as new.
guide_erase_why_title: Why you can't just restore your backup
guide_erase_why_restore: A backup from before supervision brings your data back, but it also turns supervision off.
guide_erase_why_remove: Without supervision, the profile can be removed in Settings. On a hard day, the way out is one tap away.
guide_erase_why_apps: Without supervision, the profile can't block apps. It can only block websites.
guide_erase_icloud: So after supervising, only what syncs to iCloud comes back, like iCloud Photos, Contacts and Notes. Apps download again from the App Store.
guide_erase_backup: Back up first anyway, to iCloud or to your Mac in Finder. Restoring that backup is your way back if you change your mind.
guide_erase_app: Want to keep everything on it? The {app} supervises it without erasing, for $29 per supervision. It makes a fresh backup of your iPhone, changes one setting in it and restores it, so your data and supervision both stay.
guide_need_mac: A Mac with macOS 15.7 or later, and a cable for your iPhone.
guide_need_passwords: Your iPhone passcode and your Apple Account password.
guide_step_backup_icloud: To iCloud: on the iPhone, Settings > your name > iCloud > iCloud Backup > Back Up Now.
guide_step_backup_finder: To your Mac: plug the iPhone in and tap Trust on it. Open Finder and select the iPhone. Under Backups, choose “Back up all of the data on your iPhone to this Mac”, tick “Encrypt local backup”, then click Back Up Now.
guide_step_backup_note: Keep this backup. It is your way back if you change your mind.
guide_step_erase_body: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Erase All Content and Settings. Enter your passcode and your Apple Account password. This turns off Find My and Activation Lock, which Configurator needs. If your iPhone uses an eSIM and asks, choose to keep the eSIM.
guide_step_erase_stolen: If Stolen Device Protection is on and you are away from home, the iPhone asks for Face ID first.
guide_step_erase_hello: When the iPhone restarts, leave it on the Hello screen.
guide_step_configurator_body: Get {configurator} from the Mac App Store. It is free and made by Apple. Open it. If it shows a welcome screen, click Get Started.
guide_step_prepare_connect: Plug the iPhone into the Mac. When it shows up in Configurator, right-click it and choose Prepare.
guide_step_prepare_manual: Choose “Manual Configuration” and tick “Supervise devices”. Leave “Allow devices to pair with other computers” ticked. Leave “Add to Apple School Manager or Apple Business” unticked.
guide_step_prepare_skip: If it asks about device management, choose “Do not enroll in Device Management”. If it asks you to sign in to Apple School Manager or Apple Business, click Skip.
guide_step_prepare_org: For the organization, enter your own name. You are an organization of one. Then choose “Generate a new supervision identity”. Your Mac may ask for its password.
guide_step_prepare_setup: For Setup Assistant, choose “Don’t show any of these steps”, then click Prepare.
guide_step_prepare_done: Configurator erases the iPhone once more and brings it back supervised.
guide_step_setup_home: The iPhone opens straight to the home screen. In Settings, join Wi-Fi, and check Language & Region under General.
guide_step_setup_no_restore: Do not restore the backup from step 1. A backup from before supervision takes supervision off again.
guide_step_setup_account: In Settings, set a passcode and Face ID, and sign in with your Apple Account. What you sync to iCloud comes back on its own, like iCloud Photos, contacts, Messages in iCloud and passwords. Apps with their own backup, like WhatsApp, offer to restore it when you sign in.
guide_step_setup_find_my: Turn Find My back on in Settings > your name > Find My. It still locates the phone, but a supervised iPhone has no Activation Lock.
guide_step_setup_apps: Then install the apps you need from the App Store.
guide_step_setup_check: The top of Settings now says the iPhone is supervised.
guide_step_setup_managed: It also says “managed”. That is normal: no one manages the phone, because you skipped device management.
guide_step_build_body: Open the {builder}, pick the apps and sites to block, and download the profile. It is free.
guide_step_build_trial: The profile is permanent by default. Only erasing the iPhone takes it off. To try it first, tick Trial mode. A trial profile can be removed in Settings.
guide_step_build_by_hand: Configurator can also build a profile by hand, under File > New Profile, if you would rather set every option yourself.
guide_step_install_body: Unlock the iPhone first. Then drag the profile onto the iPhone in Configurator, or right-click the iPhone and choose Add > Profiles. A supervised iPhone usually installs the profile without asking. If it asks, open Settings and tap Install.
guide_step_install_done: The apps you blocked disappear, and the sites on your list stop loading.
guide_step_install_more: Forgot something? Build another profile and add it the same way. It adds to the one already there. A new profile can only add blocks. It cannot loosen one.
guide_undo_body: Erase the iPhone from Settings: General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Erase All Content and Settings. That takes supervision and every profile off. Then restore the backup from step 1, or set it up as new. Anything you added since then comes back only if it syncs to iCloud.

build_install_2: Select the iPhone, click Add, then Profiles, and choose the file you downloaded.
build_install_3: Keep the iPhone unlocked. A supervised iPhone usually installs the profile without asking. If it asks, open Settings and tap Install.

build_stack_note: Every download is a new profile. A second one adds to the first and cannot loosen or replace it.
build_web_allow_body: Safari opens only the sites on this list and blocks everything else.
build_web_deny_body: Hiding an app leaves its website open, so every blocked app adds its sites here. Untick a site to leave it open.
